As [shared earlier][sp], the [Open Semantic Interchange (OSI) project][osi] 
(archived) is a vendor-neutral and open-source[^ap] initiative to standardise how 
organisations exchange semantic metadata for analytics, BI[^bi], AI, and other 
use-cases (what is also called a semantic layer). It aims to allow organisations 
to define metadata on data models, tables, relationships, attributes, and 
computed metrics[^sp] in a machine-readable format once and use it across 
various tools such as Snowflake, Databricks, dbt, Tableau, and more.

[In Spring][sp], the working group involved CARTO, from the geospatial domain.  

The OSI project [has been accepted into the Apache Incubator][acc] and has 
changed its name to Apache Ossie. The old website – 
[open-semantic-interchange.org](https://open-semantic-interchange.org/) – seems 
to be defunct. From the announcement by [dbt Labs][dbt]:

> Incubating Ossie with the Apache Software Foundation ensures that it remains 
an open standard with no single controlling entity. The goal of Ossie is to 
provide industry-wide standardization of semantic data, and to that end ensuring 
that it has a vendor neutral ground to operate in is imperative.
>
> Under incubation, Ossie operates with public mailing lists, GitHub-based 
development, a formal discussion-and-vote process for spec changes, and 
committership earned through contribution rather than employer affiliation. 

The coalition behind OSI/Ossie has grown from 17 founding partners to [more than 
50 organisations][orgs] encompassing organisations such as CARTO, Databricks, 
dbt Labs, JetBrains, Microsoft, Mistral AI, NVIDIA, Qlik, and Snowflake. The new 
website is at [ossie.apache.org](https://ossie.apache.org/) where the community 
also publishes [updates][up]. Work is carried out [on GitHub][gh].

[^ap]: Under the Apache 2.0 license.
[^bi]: Business intelligence, that is the technologies and practices for 
collecting, analysing, and presenting business data (for example, in reports and 
dashboards) to support decision-making.
[^sp]: See the [earlier post][sp] for links to explanations on each of these.
